analysis.title: How can investors refocus equity exposure?
key_insights: UBS CIO holds a Neutral stance on global equities but expects gains across most global markets in 2027, backed by robust earnings growth.
AI is called a structural growth driver. UBS forecasts aggregate AI investment of USD 1tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028.

The AI debate is shifting from whether investment continues to whether it can generate adequate shareholder returns. Competition, price cuts, financing constraints and monetization challenges mean gains will be uneven.
Concentrated portfolios raise exposure to company-specific setbacks. UBS recommends reducing excess tech concentration and single-stock positions.
UBS forecasts around 15% earnings growth in both the US and Eurozone in 2027, with a robust US economy and solid labor market supporting earnings outside the AI complex.

Eurozone equities are favored because they offer similar earnings growth to US equities at lower valuations. Europe earnings growth is forecast at 15% in both 2026 and 2027, on manufacturing recovery, structural investment and operating leverage.
At sector level UBS favors industrials and health care. US equal-weight strategies can help reduce technology concentration.
The S&P 500 entered correction territory, down 11.5% from its 6 October high, led by tech. The Nasdaq is down almost 20% over the same period.

UBS suggests using market volatility to progressively rebalance in a disciplined way. Structured strategies may help investors participate or generate income when implied volatility is elevated, with capital-loss, issuer, liquidity and opportunity cost risks.
